title: The 2,200-year-old idea: add up thin strips
back: Archimedes found curved areas by adding up many small shapes. An integral is that sum, with the strips made infinitely thin.

title: Why the integral sign looks like that
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" aria-label="The letter S for summa stretched into the integral sign" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"><text x="70" y="118" font-size="96" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">S</text><path d="M112,92 H168 M158,84 L168,92 L158,100" stroke-width="2"/><text x="220" y="124" font-size="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none">∫</text><text x="70" y="172" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">summa = sum</text><text x="222" y="172" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">integral sign</text></svg>
back: Leibniz stretched S, for *summa* (sum), into ∫. He and Newton found that this sum is differentiation run backwards.

title: Where integrals work for you
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" aria-label="Speed-time graph with the area under it shaded" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"><path d="M34,150 H280 M44,160 V18" stroke-width="1"/><polygon points="44,150 44,110 120,60 200,60 260,150" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity="0.3" stroke="none"/><path d="M44,110 L120,60 L200,60 L260,150" class="u" stroke-width="2"/><text x="276" y="166" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">time</text><text x="40" y="14" font-size="11" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">speed</text><text x="150" y="116" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">area = distance</text></svg>
back: Area under a speed–time graph is distance. Power over time gives the units on an electricity bill; force over distance gives work.

title: Integrals of tan x and sec x
back: $\int\sec x\,dx=\log\lvert\sec x+\tan x\rvert+C$; $\int\cot x\,dx=\log\lvert\sin x\rvert+C$; $\int\operatorname{cosec}x\,dx=\log\lvert\operatorname{cosec}x-\cot x\rvert+C$.

title: 1 over (x² + a²)
back: The only one of the three rational forms that gives an inverse tangent. Do not forget the $\dfrac1a$.

title: 1 over (x² − a²)
back: For $a^2-x^2$: $\dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left\lvert\dfrac{a+x}{a-x}\right\rvert+C$. Complete the square first if there is an $x$ term.

title: 1 over √(a² − x²)
back: No $\dfrac1a$ in front. With $x^2\pm a^2$ under the root the answer is $\log\left\lvert x+\sqrt{x^2\pm a^2}\right\rvert+C$.

title: √(a² − x²)
back: The area integral for circles and ellipses. Starts with half of $x$ times the same root.

title: Integration by parts
legend: u = first function, chosen by ILATE
back: First × integral of second − integral of (derivative of first × integral of second).

title: eˣ[f(x) + f′(x)]
back: Split the bracket into a function and its derivative: $\int e^x\left(\frac1x-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)dx=\frac{e^x}{x}+C$.

title: Partial fractions
back: Repeated factor: add $\frac{B}{(x-a)^2}$. Quadratic factor: $Bx+C$ on top. Improper fraction: divide first.

title: Property: x → a + b − x
back: With lower limit 0: $\int_0^af(x)\,dx=\int_0^af(a-x)\,dx$. Apply, add the two forms, and $2I$ becomes easy.

title: Limits −a to a
tex: \begin{gathered}\int_{-a}^{a}f\,dx=2\int_0^a f\,dx\\ \text{if } f \text{ is even}\\ \int_{-a}^{a}f\,dx=0\\ \text{if } f \text{ is odd}\end{gathered}

title: Second fundamental theorem
back: No $+C$. If you substitute, change the limits too. Split the integral where a modulus changes sign.

title: Squares of sine and cosine
back: Lower the power before integrating. Products: $2\sin A\cos B=\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)$.
